rope_rotate — LLMCORE prepare op

• Data kinds: tokens → tokens

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.rope_rotate(tokens, positions=None, base: 'float' = 10000.0) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import llmcore; llmcore.rope_rotate(tokens, positions=None, base: 'float' = 10000.0) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsllmcore.get("rope_rotate"))

Usage

Rotary position encoding (RoPE) → tokens. Being a rotation, it preserves the norm.

Su et al. 2021. Each even/odd pair (x₂ᵢ, x₂ᵢ₊₁) is rotated by the angle pos · base**(−2i/d). It is a direct sum of plane rotations, so ‖RoPE(x)‖ == ‖x‖ holds exactly (measured 8.9e-16), and the inner product of 2 rotated vectors is determined only by the difference in position (shifting the absolute position 40 ways gives a spread of 8.9e-15) — the claim "relative position is embedded in the inner product" becomes the cross-check as it stands.

Args:

tokens: (T, d) float. d is even (to rotate in pairs).

positions: (T,) positions. None means 0..T−1. Non-contiguous positions (a cut-out window) can also be passed.

base: base of the angles. The larger it is, the more slowly the low axes rotate (for long contexts).

Returns:

tokens (T, d) float: rotated per pair. The norm of each row is the same as the input.
